problems.title: Destruction order
problems.statement: void f() { A a; B b; C c; }

parts.prompt: Destructor order at the end of f?

problems.solution: Locals are destroyed in reverse order of construction: c, b, a.

problems.title: Rule of what?
problems.statement: A class whose members are std::string name; std::vector<int> ids; std::unique_ptr<Impl> impl;.

parts.prompt: Which special members should you write?

options: Only if you write a destructor

problems.solution: Rule of zero. unique_ptr's deleted copy makes the implicit copy constructor deleted, so the class is move-only.

problems.title: Buffer bugs
problems.statement: The Buffer class from the thinking trace: new char[n], delete data, no copy constructor.

options: implicit copy leads to a double delete

problems.solution: No virtual destructor is needed: Buffer isn't used polymorphically.

problems.title: Temporaries
problems.statement: const std::string& r = std::string("hi") + "!"; and later std::string_view v = std::string("hi") + "!";

parts.prompt: Is r valid after the statement?
options: Yes: binding to a const& local extends the temporary's lifetime
No: string_view doesn't extend lifetime; it dangles

hints: Lifetime extension applies to references bound directly to the temporary.

problems.title: Invalidation
problems.statement: std::vector<int> v = {1, 2, 3}; int& x = v[0]; v.push_back(4); x = 7;

options: No: push_back may reallocate, so x dangles (UB)

parts.prompt: Which call would make it safe?

problems.solution: With capacity 3, adding a 4th element reallocates. Reserving enough first prevents reallocation.

problems.title: shared_ptr cost
problems.statement: Copying a shared_ptr in a hot loop on a multi-core machine.

options: an atomic increment (and an atomic decrement on destruction)

parts.prompt: Better for read-only use in a callee?
options: pass const T& (or T*) to the pointee

problems.solution: Atomic reference-count updates bounce the cache line between cores. Pass references when the callee doesn't share ownership.

problems.title: Cycles

parts.prompt: What happens when the last external shared_ptr to the parent dies?
options: Both leak: their counts stay at 1

problems.solution: weak_ptr doesn't contribute to the strong count.

problems.title: unique_ptr reset
problems.statement: In reset(T* q), why assign p_ = q before deleting the old pointer?

options: If ~T re-enters this object (e.g. through a callback), it sees a consistent state

hints: What if the deleted object's destructor touches the owner?
problems.solution: The standard specifies this order. It also makes reset(get()) mistakes less catastrophic, though still wrong.
